verdicts.claim: All four of Orb's fighter concepts are CONDITIONAL: franchise-signature mechanisms must be replaced with original ones before public use.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-019 is Open and the review marks all four CONDITIONAL, listing specific story devices (a seven-item wish, a beast stage, a fusion accessory, a food beam and others). None of the listed devices is built in sim, data, render or ui at the pinned build or HEAD. The review's own line that q3-screen replaces the 'no orbs' rule contradicts CLAUDE.md; I did not check that further.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: None. The gate is correctly open, and its cost is one Legal checklist pass on each final design.
verdicts.fix: Keep it open. Close each device as Orb picks its replacement, and get the lawyer review the document itself asks for before any store page or trailer.

verdicts.claim: Limits: these are screens, not clearance or legal advice. Searches were US-only, the USPTO was searched only for VORR and KAI, the EU/UK/Japan/WIPO registers and social handles were not checked, and a name must be re-screened before it is locked or announced.
verdicts.what_is_true: The committed log states these limits, and its Sources list covers only the 2026-09-28 wave. [fan-game title] appears only at :449 and :460 and no row uses it. RL-248 to RL-255 sit after Sources at :462-469 in HEAD (an uncommitted edit moves them back). The working title is already public in the repo name and both live page titles, while RL-024 is Medium/CONDITIONAL with no searches outside the US.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: None. It is an accurate statement of scope.
verdicts.fix: Before any store page, run name-screening stages 2 to 5 (a formal search in the US, EU, UK and Japan) on the title. Commit the table fix for RL-248 to RL-255, and drop the orphan [fan-game title] source or tie it to a row.

verdicts.claim: Orb's fighter notes, which name franchise inspirations, stay in .private/ and are never quoted into committed files; the feel reference is named only there.
verdicts.what_is_true: .private/ is git-ignored and has never been committed. But the flash-series feel reference, which vision.md:75 says is named only in .private/, is named in 6 committed public files (vision.md:199, review-log.md:432, name-screening.md:164, never-use-words.md:8, q3-screen.md, narrative/title-pitch.md:107), and 9 committed files name the main franchise. Legal rates the nod low risk, and naming an inspiration is not infringement.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low. Treated as a breach, it could prompt a history rewrite, which gains nothing in a repo that is already public.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record: reword vision.md:75 (or :199 and the narrative pitch) so the two agree, and keep franchise names to the Legal screens whose calls depend on them.

verdicts.claim: No in-progress character art on any public page, HUD mock sheets stay private, and store frames show only the build as it ships.
verdicts.what_is_true: This is Orb's marketing preference in Orb's own words (vision.md:844-850). The live holding page has no images, and /play/ shows the build's fighters, which Orb allowed. The public repo holds 351 concept files, fighter close-ups among them, under Orb's ruling that the repo stays public. Steam's rule that screenshots show gameplay only is real.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/assets/standard (accessed 2026-11-07): 'Screenshots should exclusively show the gameplay of your game.'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: As a safety rule it invites scrubbing art from a public repo or holding the site over a marketing preference.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Orb's creative and marketing direction (Marketing). Ask Orb once whether committed concept sheets in the public repo are acceptable, and keep Steam's screenshot rule in the store checklist.

verdicts.claim: The core four names (Grist, Loupe, Empress Orza, Bolus) are clear as in-game proper nouns only: no line plays on what a name means, and no title, subtitle, store tag, DLC or merchandise use without a formal search.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-211 clears the names with these conditions. At HEAD the names exist only as display rows in ui/data/fighter_names.json, they are absent from the pinned public build, and no shipped line plays on a name's meaning. The formal search before any product use is standard trademark hygiene. The Gemini model behind the names is still unrecorded.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: a meaning check on new lines, plus a formal search only if a name becomes a product name.
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a Legal condition. Record the Gemini model and brief, as the screen asks.

verdicts.claim: Standing rule: movegen-banned.json's pose, motion and energy bans bar the franchise's best-known wind-ups, beam poses, vanish steps and barrages; the generator must refuse them, the build must fail if one slips through, the rows only grow, and 'a person screens every signature frame, new vocabulary and stance tell'.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rows exist and have grown past the stated counts (s01-s09, e01-e16, k01-k06), and the pending generator refuses matching shapes. But nothing fails a build today. CI has run no job since 3c9005ac, the held lint covers only h01-h03 inside anim_check, which no workflow runs, and new rows refuse nothing until they get a machine form (legal.mjs:8-10). The 'person' who screens is the Legal AI session, and single poses carry little legal weight.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It gives false assurance that a human screens and that the build blocks lookalikes, and a growing ban list constrains Combat's generator and costs a Legal pass on every frame.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record: the Legal session screens, and some rows have no machine form, so list them. Fix CI and wire the held lint into a workflow, and treat the pose bans as originality rules under Orb's direction.

verdicts.claim: The Anti-hero's glasses stay generic: angular lenses and a pale-violet wedge glare held 0.4 s at most, at key moments only and never at a transformation break, no bridge-finger push or folded hands, no stock 'as planned' lines; five glare frames are GO and frame 3 (chamfer plates) must change or be dropped.
verdicts.what_is_true: Legal itself calls the glare trope free to use (glasses-rules.md:5), so these are originality rules. render/vfx/glare.gd implements them: a pale-violet wedge, hold capped at 24 ticks (0.4 s), blocked in transformations, charges and rubble rings, with a 200-tick cooldown, and it ships in the public build. Orb picked frame C, the bare wedge (glare.gd:3), so the open item on frame 3 is moot. I did not measure the glare's luminance.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It keeps an RL row open, and a gate condition alive, for a frame nobody uses.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-066 (Orb chose frame C) and move the glasses look rules to Art and VFX under Orb's direction.

verdicts.claim: Two extended fingers or a pointing finger as an energy hand (two_finger_point), and two fingers to the forehead or temple, are NO-GO as the franchise's beam and teleport signatures.
verdicts.what_is_true: The NO-GO stands and is held as ban row b10. two_finger_point appears in no data, sim, render or ui file at HEAD or in the pinned build, only in Legal docs, so it has already been replaced, though RL-047 still reads 'Open until it is replaced'.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: an open blocker row for a pose already gone from the data reads as an outstanding NO-GO at gates.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-047 as replaced, and keep b10 as the guard.

verdicts.claim: ADR 0007: no human author is required for any content class (ownership rated Low), but liability controls stay: originality screens, provenance records feeding the store's AI-content disclosure, third-party licence checks, and Legal review before any store page remain mandatory.
verdicts.what_is_true: The ADR says this. Its basis matches the US Copyright Office's position (Part 2 report, 2025-01-29), and Steam's content survey does require disclosure of pre-generated AI content. Provenance records exist in part (art/animation/records/, docs/narrative/pending/provenance_*.json); I did not check their coverage or the licence register. Accepting weak ownership is Orb's decision, not a safety question.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey (accessed 2026-11-07): 'created with the help of AI tools during development.'
https://www.copyright.gov/newsnet/2025/1060.html (accessed 2026-11-07): 'our conclusions turn on the centrality of human creativity to copyright.'
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: None beyond keeping records. Without them the Steam disclosure cannot be backed up.
verdicts.fix: Keep it. Before any store page, audit provenance coverage asset by asset and fill in Steam's survey from it.

verdicts.claim: Capsule art, key art, wordmark and trailer: a plain licensed font with no logo echoing a franchise, a logo look-alike screen, the two-marks stacking rule on every frame, no hero holding a sphere aloft, no hair-colour change and no placeholder names.
verdicts.what_is_true: The conditions are written as stated, and HEAD has no capsule, key art, wordmark or logo file. The font licence and the logo look-alike screen are real licence and trademark checks. The stacking, sphere and hair limits are originality rules.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: one checklist pass when a capsule is made.
verdicts.fix: Keep it on the store checklist. Hand the stacking, sphere and hair items to Art and Marketing under Orb's direction.

verdicts.claim: Energy hands, releases, deliveries, gestures and stance moves are clear, but the short beam is conditional, not yet drawn, and must be seen drawn before it goes live; a held-pose check on Legal's rules gates the animation data.
verdicts.what_is_true: The short beam is now drawn as PROVISIONAL poses (beam2.mjs:27, :39) and used in anim_fighter.gd:5360, and Legal passed the Anti-hero's thin short beam on 2026-10-16, yet RL-084 still says 'not yet drawn'. The held-pose check exists, but it covers h01-h03 only and runs inside anim_check, which no workflow runs, so it gates nothing automatically.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: The stale row suggests an undrawn item is waiting on Legal, and the word 'gates' overstates a check that is run by hand.
verdicts.fix: Legal screens the drawn snap-beam poses and closes RL-084. Correct orb-review-list.md:120 to call the held lint a local check, or wire it into CI.

verdicts.claim: 'VORR' is Low risk but CONDITIONAL: working name only, with the full name-screening process re-run at name lock. vorr.com is taken.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-003 reads as claimed, and vorr.com is registered (RDAP: 2003-05-09, GoDaddy). VORR survives only as an internal id (roster.js:6 in the JS oracle, and the wearer list at glare.gd:23). Players see PROTAGONIST/RIVAL in the pinned build and Loupe at HEAD, so VORR will never reach name lock. 'Closed' beside an open condition is only a record inconsistency.
verdicts.fix: Retire RL-003 as superseded by RL-211 (Loupe).

verdicts.claim: 'ki' is a grey zone and is replaced by 'Charge' for players. Glossary picks carry limits: Quake is label only, Cataclysm never in a title, tag or logo, and Warden and Last Witness are descriptors only, never brands.
verdicts.what_is_true: The UI change has landed. The sim still emits 'NEED 45 KI', but UiData.banner() turns ' KI' into ' CHARGE' before drawing, in the pinned build (ui_data.gd:109, ui_event_hub.gd:475) and at HEAD (ui_data.gd:132), so :403's 'still needs the UI change' is stale. Quake and Cataclysm appear only as tier labels (terms.json:6). The prototype in the repo still says KI, but it is not served.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Negligible: the contradiction it flags is stale wording.
verdicts.fix: Correct RL-015's note to say the UI rename has landed. Keep the title and tag limits on the glossary words.

verdicts.claim: The repo name Breakers-Like is Medium risk if public: rename before public and keep 'Breakers' out of the public name, description, topics and README.
verdicts.what_is_true: The condition is met: the public repo is orb-combat-ex with no description and no topics, and README has no 'Breakers' (gh api, 2026-11-07). RL-012 still reads Open. The local folder name shows up in 38 committed files as temp paths (for example d20-clips.json:18), which also exposes the Windows user name.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: an open P0 gate flag for a rename that is already done.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-012. Tools should strip local paths from committed clip lists, a privacy hygiene item.

verdicts.claim: The prototype hero's golden hair must not carry into art. Art must never choose gold hair, or a hair-colour change, as a power cue.
verdicts.what_is_true: The prototype hair is teal #22c7a9 (:185). The claimed test exists (qa/tests/tables.test.js:33-42, run by qa/run-all.js in CI, which is dead) and covers the JS harness fighters. The Godot build's fighter data uses teal and #181818 hair (data/fighters), and Art's docs keep one hair colour in every form (anti-hero-concepts.md:27). I did not check every render palette.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Low: one open row, which only needs closing once the art bible fixes the palette.
verdicts.fix: Close the art-bible part once the palette is final, and add the gold-hue test to the Godot fighter data, not only the JS harness.

batch_notes: The inventory's line numbers match committed HEAD. The working tree holds an uncommitted edit to review-log.md that moves RL-247 to RL-255 into the table (RL-247 is new and uncommitted).

Several Legal rows stay open after the fix landed elsewhere: RL-012 (the repo was renamed), RL-047 (the pose is gone from data), RL-066 (frame 3 is not used), RL-084 (the beam is drawn), and RL-015's 'needs the UI change' (the rename has landed). The log has no step for closing rows.
The pose and look bans are mostly Orb's originality line. Their enforcement claims rest on CI that is dead and on anim_check, which no workflow runs.
